title: Sumerian city-states
summary: Sumerian cities such as Uruk, Ur and Eridu developed in southern Mesopotamia between the 4th and 3rd millennia BCE. Their city-states were each ruled by a monarch and fought over arable land and water rights until Sargon of Akkad conquered the region. Sumer is recognized as the birthplace of many firsts of civilization, including writing and the city, and Ur-Nammu wrote the first legal code in Sumer.

uncertainty.note: Early Dynastic period dated c. 2900 to c. 2350/2334 BCE when Sargon of Akkad conquered the region; earlier urban growth began in the 4th millennium BCE.

as_recorded.value: between the 4th and the 3rd millennium BCE
